info.title: GlassFrog API v5 (Beta)
info.description:
The GlassFrog API v5 provides programmatic access to your organization's
Holacracy structure — roles, accountabilities, domains, assignments, and more.

> **⚠️ Beta Notice:** This API is in beta. Breaking changes may occur.
> See the **Release Notes** section at the end of this document for updates.

## Authentication

All requests require an API v5 key. Send it in either the `X-Auth-Token`
header or the `Authorization` header as a Bearer credential — the two are
equivalent. API v5 keys are distinct from v3 keys and must be generated
separately.

```
X-Auth-Token: your_v5_api_key_here
```
```
Authorization: Bearer your_v5_api_key_here
```

The `Authorization: Bearer` form carries the same static API key — it is
NOT OAuth: there is no expiry, no scopes, and no refresh. It exists so
hosted clients that cannot set a custom header (for example the Claude
Console managed-agent and Messages API MCP connectors) can still connect.

If both headers are sent, `X-Auth-Token` takes precedence; an invalid
`X-Auth-Token` is rejected rather than falling back to `Authorization`.

Each API key is scoped to a single organization and person; permissions
follow the caller's membership in that organization.

## Pagination

List endpoints use cursor-based pagination. Use `per_page` and `cursor` to
page through results. Pass `cursor` the `next_cursor` value from the
previous response.

Page size limits belong to the endpoint, not to the API as a whole. Most
endpoints default to 100 records per page and allow at most 500. Some use
lower values. `GET /search` defaults to 25 and allows at most 100. Read
`meta.pagination.per_page` in the response to see the size the server
applied.

Values above an endpoint's maximum return `400 Bad Request` with a `message`
explaining the limit — callers should not assume the server silently clamped.
Blank, zero, negative, or non-numeric values fall back to the endpoint's
default.

```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "per_page": 100,
      "has_next_page": true,
      "next_cursor": "role_abc123..."
    }
  }
}
```

### Result order

List endpoints return records in the order the server stored them. The
oldest stored record comes first. New records are added at the end. This
order is stable.

Paging is separate from order. Each endpoint defines its own cursor, so a
record can appear on more than one page. Dedupe by `id` as you page.

Storage order is not the same as the `created_at` field. Some records were
given a `created_at` value after they were stored, so the two can differ.
Sort the records yourself if you need them in `created_at` order.

`GET /search` is the exception. It returns results ranked by relevance.

### Known exception: `GET /roles/{role_id}/skills`

This endpoint reads the cursor from `after`, not from `cursor`. Sending
`cursor` to it returns the first page again. Use `after` on this endpoint.
Every other list endpoint uses `cursor`. This difference is a known
defect. It is not fixed yet.

## Unrecognised query parameters

The API ignores query parameters it does not recognise. It does not reject
them. A misspelled or wrong parameter name is dropped, and the request
still succeeds. You get no error and no warning.

This matters most for pagination. Send the cursor under a name the endpoint
does not read, and the API returns the first page again, with
`has_next_page` still `true`. Two failures follow:

- A loop that pages until `has_next_page` is `false` never ends.
- A caller that reads one page believes it read the whole collection. It
  sees only the records on the first page. The rest are never returned.

To confirm you are paging, check that each page returns different ids.

## Includes

Detail endpoints support `?include=` to embed related resources.
Pass a comma-separated list of valid include names.

## Legacy IDs (transition-only)

> **⚠️ Temporary migration bridge — will be removed.** The `legacy_id`
> field described here exists solely to ease the v3→v5 transition and
> **retires when the v3 API retires.** Do not build durable integrations on
> it; use the v5 TypeID (`id`) as the stable identifier.

v5 identifies resources by opaque TypeIDs (e.g. `org_1a2b…`, `role_9f8e…`),
which intentionally differ from the v3 sequential numeric IDs (e.g. the org
id `38655` shown in the web UI). To help integrators migrating from v3
correlate the two, pass `?include_legacy_id=true` on any standard resource
endpoint (and `/me`). Each resource in the response then carries an extra
`legacy_id` field holding its v3 sequential integer id:

```
GET /api/v5/me?include_legacy_id=true
→ { "data": { "organization": { "id": "org_1a2b…", "legacy_id": 38655, … } } }
```

Notes:
- **Opt-in and off by default** — `legacy_id` is omitted unless the param is
  passed, keeping the default v5 contract free of v3 coupling.
- **Actors backed by agents return `null`** — agents have no v3 representation.
- Applies to the standard resource list/show endpoints and `/me`. Nested
  `?include=` embeds and the cross-model `search` / agent-`context`
  aggregation endpoints do not carry `legacy_id`.

## Optimistic Concurrency (ETags)

GET responses for mutable resources include an `ETag` header — a hash of the
resource's current state. To prevent stale writes, send the ETag back on
PUT/PATCH via the `If-Match` header:

```
GET /api/v5/notes/rnot_abc123
→ ETag: "a1b2c3..."

PATCH /api/v5/notes/rnot_abc123
If-Match: "a1b2c3..."
→ 200 OK          (ETag matched — write accepted)
→ 409 Conflict     (resource changed since your read — re-fetch and retry)
```

If `If-Match` is omitted, the update proceeds unconditionally (last-write-wins).
This keeps it simple for consumers who don't need concurrency protection.

## Errors

Errors follow the RFC 9457 Problem Details shape (the backward-compatible
2023 successor to RFC 7807) and are served with
`Content-Type: application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "Not Found"
}
```

`type`, `title`, `status`, and `detail` are always present. Additional
members ("extensions" in RFC 9457 terms) may appear alongside them.

## Rate Limiting

API requests are rate-limited per organization on a rolling 1-hour window.
Limits depend on your plan:

| Plan | Limit |
|------|-------|
| Free / Restricted | 50 requests / hour |
| Premium | `member_count × 500` requests / hour |

Every response includes rate limit headers:

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests allowed in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix epoch timestamp when the window resets |

When the limit is exceeded, the API returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a
`Retry-After` header and an RFC 9457 Problem Details body:

```json
{
  "type": "about:blank",
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 42 seconds."
}
```

## Release Notes

Curated highlights of notable changes and clarifications. This section is the
canonical changelog for API v5 — check here for updates.

### Beta (current)

- **Focus & election data comes via `?include=assignments`.** A node's
  assignments — carrying focus and election data — are embedded by requesting
  `GET /roles/{id}/tree?include=assignments`. Note that `?include=members`
  returns bare fillers *without* focus or election data; use
  `?include=assignments` when you need focus.
- **Assignments API surface.** Assignments are accessed through the nested
  collection paths `GET`/`POST /roles/{id}/assignments` and
  `GET /actors/{id}/assignments`, plus `PATCH`/`DELETE /assignments/{id}` for
  a single assignment. There is no standalone `GET /assignments` collection
  endpoint — the tree's `?include=assignments` already returns every focus in
  one call.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of roles in the organization. Each role includes
its accountabilities, domains, fillers, and flags inline. Use filters to
narrow results by parent role or assigned person.

parameters.name: parent_role_id
parameters.description: Filter to roles within a specific parent role.

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Filter to roles assigned to a specific person.

parameters.name: has_subroles
parameters.description:
Filter by whether a role has sub-roles. `true` returns only roles
with sub-roles; `false` returns only leaf roles. Omit to
return all roles.

get.description:
Returns a single role by its ID. Use `?include=` to embed related
resources such as assignments, sub-roles, parent role, policies, or notes.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

get.description:
Returns the immediate child roles of a role (its subroles).
For leaf roles with no subroles, returns an empty array.

Navigate the org hierarchy by walking this tree:
```
GET /roles                          → top-level roles
GET /roles/:id/subroles            → what's inside this role
GET /roles/:id/subroles?include=subroles  → two levels deep
```

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include on each sub-role.

200.description: A paginated list of child roles.

get.summary: List actors filling a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns actors (humans and agents) filling any direct sub-role of this
role. One level of nesting. Cross-linked assignments are excluded.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404. Same response shape as `GET /actors`.

Use `?kind=human` to filter to human actors only, or use the
`/roles/{id}/subroles/people` alias.

200.description: A paginated list of subrole actors.

get.summary: List people filling a role's subroles
get.description:
Alias for `GET /roles/{id}/subroles/actors?kind=human`. Returns only
human actors (people) filling any direct sub-role of this role.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404. Same response shape as `GET /actors`.

200.description: A paginated list of people filling subroles.

get.summary: List projects rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns projects owned by any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/projects`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

get.summary: List actions rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns actions owned by any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/actions`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

get.summary: List policies rolled up across a role's subroles
get.description:
Returns policies attached to any direct sub-role of this role. Same
response shape as `GET /roles/:id/policies`. One level of nesting.

Only available on expanded roles (where `has_subroles` is `true`).
Leaf roles return 404.

get.summary: Get the full subtree rooted at a role
get.description:
Returns the complete role hierarchy below (and including) the
requested root role, as a single nested tree node. Useful for org-chart
rendering and for agents orienting to a branch of the organization in
one call.

The per-node shape is "light" by default (id, name, purpose,
parent_role_id, has_subroles, flags, children). Use `?include=` to
add `accountabilities`, `domains`, `members` (fillers), and/or
`assignments` (with focus and election data) to every node.
Policies, notes, and skills — which are often large —
are not offered as tree-level includes; fetch them via `/roles/{id}`
for a specific role.

**Recursion is intentional** and the whole point of this endpoint,
in contrast to `/roles/{id}/subroles` which returns only direct
children.

**Pagination:** not supported. GlassFrog organizations are small
enough (typically 100–500 roles) that returning the full tree in one
response is the simpler and more useful design. Use `?depth=` when
you need to bound response size.

**Caching:** responses carry an `ETag` header whose fingerprint
combines the maximum `updated_at` across the subtree with the
requester's authorization digest. Send `If-None-Match` on subsequent
requests to receive a `304 Not Modified` when nothing visible has
changed.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description:
Maximum depth of descendants to return. `0` returns the root
node alone with no children; `1` returns the root plus its
direct children; and so on. Omit for the full subtree.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of extra per-node fields. Unknown values are
silently ignored.

200.description: The full subtree rooted at the requested role.

304.description: Not Modified. The client's `If-None-Match` matches the current fingerprint.

get.description:
Convenience alias for `GET /roles/{id}/tree` with the requester's
organization's anchor role as the root — i.e., "the whole org". All
query parameters and response semantics match `/roles/{id}/tree`.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description:
Maximum depth of descendants to return. `0` returns the root
node alone; `1` returns root plus direct children; and so on.
Omit for the full subtree.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of extra per-node fields to include on
each tree node: `accountabilities`, `domains`, `members`,
`assignments`.

200.description: The full org tree rooted at the anchor role.

304.description: Not Modified. The client's `If-None-Match` matches the current fingerprint.

get.description:
Returns everything an agent (or person) needs to fill a role — structured
organizational context in a single API call. The response is a hypermedia
document: full content for critical items (identity, role definition, skills),
indexes with API links for everything else (policies, notes, projects).

**Progressive disclosure:** Indexed items include a `url` field pointing to
the full-detail API endpoint. Call those endpoints for complete content.

**Agent identity:** The `agent` section is only present when the API key
belongs to an agent-kind actor. Human actors receive all other sections.

200.description: The full context for filling this role.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of actors (humans and agents) in the organization.
Use `?kind=` to filter by type. The `/people` and `/agents` aliases apply
the kind filter automatically.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to actors filling a specific role.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Filter by exact email address (case-insensitive). Returns actors matching the given email within the caller's organization.

post.summary: Invite a person to the organization
post.description:
Creates a new person and membership in the organization (or adds an existing
person by email). Sends an invitation email. Requires org admin.

get.description:
Returns a single actor by ID. Accepts both `per_` (human) and `agt_` (agent)
prefixed IDs. Use `?include=` to embed roles or assignments.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

patch.description:
Updates a person's name, email, or admin status. Org admins can update
any member; non-admins can only update themselves.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

delete.summary: Remove a person from the organization
delete.description:
Removes the person's membership in the organization, along with all
role assignments, unaccepted proposals, and taggings. The person record
itself is deactivated if they have no remaining memberships.
Requires org admin.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The actor's unique identifier (per_ or agt_ prefix).

get.description:
Returns the authenticated actor's own record, bundled with organization
and membership. This is typically the first call an API consumer makes
to orient itself.

Use `?include=roles` to embed the roles the requester fills in the
response — saving the follow-up call to `/me/roles` when a client
needs both identity and role context.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to embed.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of roles the requester fills via a primary,
non-discarded assignment. Same response shape as `GET /roles`.

200.description: A paginated list of the requester's roles.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of projects owned by roles the requester
fills (primary assignments). Use `?status=` to filter.

Returns a paginated list of actions owned by roles the requester
fills (primary assignments). Use `?status=` to filter.

Self-context for the authenticated caller, in one call: the full list of
roles the caller fills, and — with `?role=role_xxx` — that role's
definition, governance context, and org skills.

Serves any authenticated caller. The agent-identity section (name,
description, SOUL-style context blob, configuration) and agent-level
skills (by ID — fetch full content via `/skills/{id}`) are present
**only when the caller is an agent**; a human caller receives the roles
and role-context sections without an `agent` section.

Analogous to `GET /agents/{id}/context` where the id is the caller's own
agent, but scoped to whoever is authenticated.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Optional role API ID. When provided, the response includes the role's definition, governance context, and org skills index.

get.description:
Returns an agent's identity orientation — identity (name, description,
SOUL-style context blob), configuration, agent-level skills (by ID),
and the full list of roles the agent fills.

Optionally pass `?role=role_xxx` to also include that role's definition,
governance context, and org skills — one call for full context.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Optional role API ID. When provided, the response includes the role's definition, governance context, and org skills index.

get.description: Convenience alias for `GET /actors?kind=human`.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to people filling a specific role.

200.description: A paginated list of human actors.

post.summary: Invite a person (alias)
post.description: Convenience alias for `POST /actors`.

get.description: Convenience alias for `GET /actors/{id}`.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

delete.description: Convenience alias for `DELETE /actors/{id}`.

get.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Convenience alias for `GET /actors?kind=agent`.
Returns 403 when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to agents filling a specific role.

200.description: A paginated list of agent actors.

get.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Convenience alias for `GET /actors/{id}`.
Returns 403 when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

get.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Returns a paginated list of skills in the
organization. Skills are knowledge documents that can be attached to
roles and agents. Use `?role_id=` to filter to skills linked to a
specific role. Use `?tags[]=foo&tags[]=bar` to filter to skills tagged
with ALL of the listed names (AND semantics, case-insensitive). Returns
403 when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to skills linked to a specific role.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Filter to skills tagged with ALL of the supplied tag names (case-insensitive). The well-known `specialist` tag marks a skill as invokable by a sub-agent.

post.summary: Create a skill
post.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Creates a new skill in the organization.
Requires agents to be enabled for the organization. Returns 403 when
the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

**Content size limit.** `content` has a maximum size in characters.
Content over the limit returns 422 and is not saved. The limit exists
because an agent reads a skill in a single response, and an oversized
skill cannot be delivered. The 422 body names the submitted size, the
limit, and the configuration key that set the limit, in the
`content_length`, `max_content_length`, and `limit_config_key` members.
Split the skill into smaller skills to save it.

get.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Returns a single skill by its ID,
including the full markdown body. Use `?include=roles` to embed the
roles linked to this skill. Returns 403 when the `ai_integration`
flag is not enabled for the organization.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of related resources to include.

200.description: A single skill with full body.

patch.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Updates the name and/or content of an
existing skill. Returns 403 when the `ai_integration` flag is not
enabled for the organization.

Supports optimistic concurrency via `If-Match`. When present, the
update only proceeds if the ETag matches the current resource state.
Omit `If-Match` for unconditional (last-write-wins) updates.

**Content size limit.** `content` has a maximum size in characters.
Content over the limit returns 422 and is not saved. The 422 body names
the submitted size, the limit, and the configuration key that set the
limit, in the `content_length`, `max_content_length`, and
`limit_config_key` members. Split the skill into smaller skills to save
it.

delete.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Soft-deletes a skill. The skill is no
longer visible but retained in the database. Returns 403 when the
`ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

get.summary: List skills linked to a role
get.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Returns the skills currently linked to the
given role, including each skill's full markdown body. Returns 403 when
the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

200.description: A paginated list of skills linked to the role.

post.summary: Link a skill to a role
post.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Links an existing skill to a role.
Idempotent — linking an already-linked skill is a no-op and still
returns 201. Returns 403 when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled
for the organization.

delete.summary: Unlink a skill from a role
delete.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Unlinks a skill from a role. Returns 403
when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

post.summary: Link a skill to an agent
post.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Links an existing skill to an agent so the
skill loads into that agent's session context. Idempotent — linking an
already-linked skill is a no-op and still returns 201. Returns 403 when
the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

context_scope.description: Optional. Controls which of the agent's session contexts load this skill. Defaults to `global`. Unrecognized values are ignored (the link is created with the default scope).

201.description: Skill linked to the agent successfully. No response body.

delete.summary: Unlink a skill from an agent
delete.description:
**Requires AI Integration.** Unlinks a skill from an agent. Returns 403
when the `ai_integration` flag is not enabled for the organization.

get.description:
Returns all primary assignments for the given role. Base response
always includes `role_id` and `actor_id` pointers. Default include
is `actor` (the full actor object). Use `?include=` to control
which related objects are embedded.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related objects to embed.
Default: `actor` (when accessed via `/roles/{role_id}/assignments`).

post.summary: Assign an actor to a role
post.description:
Creates a new assignment, assigning a person or agent to the specified role.
Authorization follows the same governance rules as the UI. The response
includes the `actor` object by default.

actor_id.description: The person or agent ID to assign.

get.description:
Returns all primary role assignments for the given actor (person or agent).
Base response always includes `role_id` and `actor_id` pointers. Default
include is `role` (the full role object). Use `?include=` to control
which related objects are embedded.

parameters.name: actor_id
parameters.description: The actor's API ID (per_ or agt_ prefix).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related objects to embed.
Default: `role` (when accessed via `/actors/{actor_id}/assignments`).

patch.description:
Updates mutable fields on an existing assignment (e.g. focus area).
Cannot change the assigned person or role.
Elected-role assignments cannot be updated.

delete.description:
Removes an assignment (un-assigns a person or agent from a role).
Authorization follows governance rules.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of actions owned by this role.
Use `?status=` to filter by action status (incomplete, waiting, archived, etc.).

post.summary: Create an action on a role
post.description: Creates a new action owned by the specified role.

get.description: Returns a single action by its ID, including full detail fields.

200.description: A single action with full detail.

patch.description: Updates the description, status, or other fields of an existing action.

delete.description: Soft-deletes an action. The action is no longer visible but retained in the database.

post.summary: Mark an action as completed
post.description:
Sets the action's status to `completed`. Idempotent — calling on an
already-completed action returns 200 with no state change.

delete.description:
Resets the action's status to `current`. Idempotent — calling on an
already-current action returns 200 with no state change.

get.summary: List checklist items for a role
get.description:
Returns a paginated list of checklist items assigned to this role.
Use `?frequency=` to filter by frequency (Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly).

200.description: A paginated list of checklist items.

post.summary: Create a checklist item on a role
post.description: Creates a new checklist item assigned to the specified role.

get.description: Returns a single checklist item by its ID, including full detail fields.

200.description: A single checklist item with full detail.

patch.description: Updates the description, frequency, or other fields of an existing checklist item.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a checklist item. The item is no longer visible but retained in the database.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of metrics assigned to this role.
Use `?frequency=` to filter by frequency (Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly).

post.summary: Create a metric on a role
post.description: Creates a new metric assigned to the specified role.

get.description: Returns a single metric by its ID, including full detail fields.

200.description: A single metric with full detail.

patch.description: Updates the description, frequency, or other fields of an existing metric.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a metric. The metric is no longer visible but retained in the database.

get.description:
Returns tensions sensed by this role (column `impacted_role_id =
role.id`; the column name is historical — semantically the role here
is the sensing role, matching the in-app "Sensed by Role" label and
the `tensions.react.sensed_by_role` i18n key). Use `?status=` to
filter by lifecycle state.

post.summary: Capture a tension about a role
post.description:
Captures a new tension. The requester is the sensing person
(`sensed_by`); the path `role_id` is the sensing role (stored as
`impacted_role_id` for historical reasons). Tensions captured this
way are not bound to a meeting.

get.summary: List tensions across a role's direct subroles
get.description:
Roll-up across the anchor role's direct children only — one level of
nesting, not a transitive closure. Mirrors the GF-2161 subroles roll-up
pattern. Anchor role must be expanded (`has_subroles: true`); leaf
roles return 404.

200.description: A paginated list of tensions sensed by the anchor's direct sub-roles.

get.description: Returns a single tension by its ID, including full detail fields.

200.description: A single tension with full detail.

patch.description:
Updates the body, label, status, or meeting_type of an existing tension.
Status transitions (e.g. to `archived`) are allowed here; automatic
status computation still runs on save.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the tension (sets `discarded_at`). Proposals associated
with the tension are not cascaded; delete those separately if needed.

**Not idempotent in the REST-strict sense.** First DELETE on a live
tension returns 204; subsequent calls return 404 (an already-discarded
tension is indistinguishable from a never-existed one). Treat
404-following-204 as success.

get.description: Returns the policies governing the inside of this role.
Returns a single policy by its ID, including the full body.

200.description: A single policy with full body.

get.description: Returns the domains controlled by this role.

Returns a single domain by its ID. Use `?include=policies` to embed
policies scoped to this domain.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of notes on a role. Notes include title,

post.summary: Create a note on a role
post.description:
Creates a new note on the specified role. The creator is tracked via
the API key's associated person.

**Agent token restriction:** Agent-actor tokens cannot set
`permissions.view` to `public` (returns 403). Only human-held
tokens may set public visibility.

**Content size limit, by author.** `body` has a maximum size in
characters, and the limit is enforced differently depending on who is
writing. An agent-held token is rejected with 422 when `body` is over
the limit, because an agent reads a note in a single response and an
oversized note cannot be delivered. A human-held token is not rejected:
the note saves, and the response carries a `warnings` array saying the
note is too large for an agent to read. A request whose author cannot be
determined is treated as an agent and is rejected.

The 422 body names the submitted size, the limit, and the configuration
key that set the limit, in the `content_length`, `max_content_length`,
and `limit_config_key` members. Split the note into smaller notes to
save it.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of notes across the whole organization,

parameters.name: title

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description:
Limit to notes on this role. When present, matches the behavior of
`GET /roles/{role_id}/notes`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match across title and body.

200.description: A single note with full content.

patch.description:
Updates the title and/or body of an existing note.

Supports optimistic concurrency via `If-Match`. When present, the
update only proceeds if the ETag matches the current resource state.
Omit `If-Match` for unconditional (last-write-wins) updates.

**Agent token restriction:** Agent-actor tokens cannot set
`permissions.view` to `public` (returns 403). Only human-held
tokens may set public visibility.

**Content size limit, by author.** `body` has a maximum size in
characters, and the limit is enforced differently depending on who is
writing. An agent-held token is rejected with 422 when `body` is over
the limit. A human-held token is not rejected: the note saves, and the
response carries a `warnings` array saying the note is too large for an
agent to read. A request whose author cannot be determined is treated as
an agent and is rejected.

The 422 body names the submitted size, the limit, and the configuration
key that set the limit, in the `content_length`, `max_content_length`,
and `limit_config_key` members. Split the note into smaller notes to
save it.

Direct children only; per-record auth scoping still applies (a
caller who can see the project may not see every sub-project or
action under it).

Each value mirrors the name of its sub-endpoint and the key

get.description:
Returns proposals visible to the caller. Supports filtering by
status, circle (via `role_id`), and date ranges. Response summary
stats only — no per-person attribution.

parameters.name: role_id
parameters.description: Filter to proposals in the circle supported by this role.

parameters.name: proposer_id
parameters.description: Filter to proposals created by this person.

parameters.name: proposed_after
parameters.description: Only proposals with `proposed_at` on or after this timestamp.

parameters.name: accepted_after
parameters.description: Only proposals with `accepted_at` on or after this timestamp.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response.

post.summary: Create a governance proposal (draft)
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Creates a proposal in `draft`
state, anchored to an existing tension. Each entry in `changes` is a
governance command (create role, add accountability, etc.) applied
atomically at acceptance time. Returns 403 when async proposals are
not enabled.

Advancing the proposal to circulation happens via a separate action
call: `POST /proposals/{id}/propose`.

get.description:
Returns a proposal with its changes, response summary stats, and the
list of transitions the caller may invoke on it right now
(`available_transitions`). Per-person response attribution is
intentionally not exposed.

post.summary: Advance a draft proposal into circulation
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Advances a `draft` proposal
to `proposed_outside_meeting` (the shortcut-path circulation state)
and auto-registers the proposer's implicit `no_objection` response.
Returns 403 when async proposals are not enabled.

The backend dispatches `propose` to the appropriate internal path
(shortcut / meeting-queue / CL-forward / etc.) based on circle + org
config. Today only the shortcut path exists; future config-driven
paths will share this same API surface (callers don't choose the path
— the org's config does).

Allowed when the caller appears in `available_transitions` for this
proposal — typically the proposer of a `draft` proposal.

Implications:
  * Notifications fire (per the existing
    `Notifications::NotifyNewAsyncProposal` chain — Slack /
    email / etc., depending on the circle's notifications config).
  * `response_deadline` is set from the circle's
    `proposal_auto_accept_day_limit`.
  * Proposer's implicit `no_objection` is recorded, but is **excluded**
    from `received_response_count` (which counts only *expected*
    responders) — the proposer's own consent can never satisfy the
    auto-accept quota.

post.summary: Withdraw a circulating proposal back to draft
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Returns a
`proposed_outside_meeting` or `escalated` proposal to `draft`.
Allowed for the proposer (and admins) when the proposal appears in
`available_transitions`. Returns 403 when async proposals are not
enabled.

Implications:
  * All existing `proposal_responses` are deleted (responders will
    need to re-respond if the proposal is later re-proposed).
  * `proposed_at` and `response_deadline` are cleared.
  * The proposal can be re-edited and re-proposed.

post.summary: Record a circle member's response to a proposal
post.description:
**Premium — requires async proposals.** Returns 403 when async
proposals are not enabled.

Circle members post one of two values during the consent window:

* `no_objection` — willing to let the proposal pass as written. When
  every expected responder has `no_objection`, the cron auto-accepts.

* `bring_to_meeting` — wants to discuss the proposal in a live
  governance meeting rather than let it circulate to auto-acceptance.
  This is NOT a retracted or formally-objected-to claim; the response
  persists on the proposal and blocks auto-acceptance. When the
  circle's agenda is ready, the proposal transitions to `escalated`
  for live discussion.

One response per person per proposal (422 on second attempt).

get.description:
Returns the channels in the caller's organization. Channels are
org-open: any org member can read and post to any channel. Each
channel is a 1:1 wrapper around a Role, which defines the channel's
audience (its members, used for notifications), not an access wall:

* **Circle role** — members are the circle's role-fillers (group
  chat semantics).
* **Leaf role** — members are the role's own filler(s) (DM-like).

Membership in either case is derived dynamically from current
assignments. Channels for a circle the caller participates in
are provisioned lazily on first list/show; leaf-role channels
are provisioned lazily on direct access.

Returns a single channel by its api_id. For convenience, the bound
role's api_id is also accepted (1:1 mapping), lazy-provisioning
the channel row if it didn't exist yet.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The channel's `chn_…` id, or the bound role's `role_…` id.

post.summary: Mark a channel read
post.description:
Advances the caller's read watermark on the channel to now (never
rewinds). Unread state is computed from the caller's newest
watermark — see the `viewer_last_read_at` / `viewer_unread_count`
fields on Channel.

Optionally scope the watermark to one of the caller's roles via
`role` — multi-role actors (typically agents) can track which of
their roles have caught up. The caller must currently fill the
role (422 otherwise).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The channel's `chn_…` id, or the bound role's `role_…` id.

role.description: Optional role api_id to scope the watermark to.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of messages in a channel, oldest stored
first. Use `cursor` + `per_page` for pagination. Soft-deleted
messages are omitted.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The channel's id (accepts channel or role api_id).

post.summary: Post a message to a channel
post.description:
Creates a new message in the channel.

Agents must post as a specific role via `from_role`. Humans may
omit `from_role` when they fill exactly one role in the channel's
circle; otherwise it must be specified.

(Notification fan-out for channel messages arrives in a follow-up
release on the event substrate; unread state is watermark-based —
see `POST /channels/{id}/read`.)

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The channel's id (accepts channel or role api_id).

patch.description:
Edits a message body. Author-only. Sets `edited_at` so clients can
render an edited marker — messages carry no further revision
history by design.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes a message. Author-only. Replies keep their threading
pointers; deleted messages are omitted from lists.

BearerAuth.description:
The same GlassFrog API v5 key, sent in the `Authorization` header as
`Authorization: Bearer <your_v5_api_key>`. Provided as an alias to
`X-Auth-Token` for hosted clients that cannot send a custom header.

This is an API key transported in the `Authorization` header — NOT
OAuth Bearer semantics. The value is your static v5 API key: it does
not expire, carry scopes, or support refresh.

Precedence: if both `X-Auth-Token` and `Authorization: Bearer` are
sent, `X-Auth-Token` is used. An invalid `X-Auth-Token` is rejected
and never falls back to `Authorization`.

ETag.description:
Hash of the resource's current state. Pass this value back as
`If-Match` on subsequent PUT/PATCH requests to enable optimistic
concurrency checking.

RateLimitLimit.description: Maximum requests allowed in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix epoch timestamp when the current window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (present on 429 responses).

PerPage.name: per_page
PerPage.description: Number of results per page (1–500, default 100). Values above the maximum return `400 Bad Request`; blank, zero, negative, or non-numeric values fall back to the default of 100.

Locale.name: locale
Locale.description:
Override the response locale. Affects localized fields such as core
role names. Resolution order: this param > subdomain > org default >
app default (en).

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
ETag from a previous GET response. When present, the server checks
that the resource has not been modified since your read. If the ETag
is stale, a 409 Conflict is returned. Omit this header for
unconditional (last-write-wins) updates.

Q.name: q
Q.description:
Full-text search filter. Matches against the resource's searchable text
fields using Postgres full-text search (`simple` + `unaccent`). Supports
Google-style syntax: `marketing -intern`, `"exact phrase"`, `foo OR bar`.
Composes with other filters (all AND'd together). Empty or whitespace-only
values are ignored. Malformed queries return no rows rather than an error.

IncludeLegacyId.name: include_legacy_id
IncludeLegacyId.description:
**Transition-only.** When `true`, each resource in the response
additionally carries a `legacy_id` field — its v3 sequential integer id
— so v3-keyed integrators can correlate v5 TypeIDs with the numeric IDs
they already hold during migration. Default is off (`legacy_id` is
omitted unless explicitly requested).

This is a temporary v3→v5 bridge and **NOT a permanent part of the v5
contract**: it retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs
(transition-only)" section in the API overview. Applies to the standard
resource list/show endpoints and `/me`; nested `?include=` embeds are
out of scope.

next_cursor.description: Present when `has_next_page` is true. Pass as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page.

description.description: For structural (constitutional) accountabilities, resolved from the Holacracy Constitution in the request locale. For custom accountabilities, the org-defined description.
description.example: Defining coding standards for the team

is_structural.description: True for constitutional accountabilities defined by the Holacracy Constitution (e.g., Facilitator's meeting facilitation duties). False for org-defined custom accountabilities.

description.description: For structural (constitutional) domains, resolved from the Holacracy Constitution in the request locale. For custom domains, the org-defined description.

is_structural.description: True for constitutional domains defined by the Holacracy Constitution. False for org-defined custom domains.

legacy_id.description: **Transition-only.** The role's v3 sequential integer id, present ONLY when `?include_legacy_id=true` is passed. A v3→v5 migration bridge for correlating TypeIDs with the numeric IDs integrators already hold; NOT a permanent part of the v5 contract — this field retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs" section in the API overview.

name.description:
Localized display name. For core roles, applies the organization's
custom term overrides first, then locale-based translation (via
`?locale=` param, subdomain, or org default). Custom roles pass
through unchanged.

purpose.example: Steering the role toward its purpose

parent_role_id.description: ID of the parent role. Null for anchor roles.

original_role_id.description:
ID of the role this role derives from — its original role.
Non-null on linked roles (which surface `linked` in `flags`) and
focus roles; `null` for all other roles. A cross-linked role
appears as two v5 records with different `id`s; the linked record
points here at its original, letting a consumer correlate the two.

has_subroles.description: Whether this role is expanded with subroles.

flags.description:
Classification flags. `structural` = core Holacracy role,
`elected` = filled by election, `linked` = cross-linked from another role.

fillers.description: People and agents currently filling this role.

tags.description: Tag names applied to this role.

skills.description: Present when `?include=skills` is requested. Returns skill summaries (no `content`); fetch full content on demand via `GET /skills/{id}`.

TreeNode.description:
A role in the tree response. `children` is always present (possibly
empty). `accountabilities`, `domains`, `fillers`, and `assignments`
are present only when their corresponding `?include=` value is set.

parent_role_id.description:
ID of the parent role. Null for the anchor role. Present on every
node even though nesting is already conveyed by `children`, so
that consumers who flatten the tree to a list retain the edge.

original_role_id.description:
ID of the role this node derives from — its original role.
Non-null on linked roles (which surface `linked` in `flags`) and
focus roles; `null` for all other roles.

children.description:
Direct children of this node, each of which is itself a
`TreeNode`. Empty array when the node is a leaf, when `?depth`
truncates beneath it, or when all children are hidden by
authorization.

A role assignment. `role_id` and `actor_id` are always present.
Use `?include=actor` or `?include=role` to embed the full related object.

role_id.description: The role that controls this domain.

view.description: Who can see this record. Resolved based on the org's public/private status (e.g., `visible_to_all` on a public org reports as `public`, on a private org as `org_member`).

Surfaced on `/me`. A v3→v5 migration bridge for correlating TypeIDs with the numeric IDs integrators already hold; NOT a permanent part of the v5 contract — this field retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs" section in the API overview.

Membership.description: A person's membership in an organization.

legacy_id.description: **Transition-only.** The membership's v3 sequential integer id, present ONLY when `?include_legacy_id=true` is passed. A v3→v5 migration bridge; NOT a permanent part of the v5 contract — this field retires when the v3 API retires. See the "Legacy IDs" section in the API overview.

MeResponse.description: Authenticated actor bundled with org context, wrapped in the standard v5 envelope.

roles.description: Present when `?include=roles` is requested. Same shape as `GET /roles`.

AgentContextResponse.description:
Self / agent context orientation. Returned by `GET /me/context` and
`GET /agents/{id}/context`. Filled roles are inlined so one call
provides enough context to orient. The `agent` section is present only
when the subject is an agent — `GET /me/context` omits it for human
callers; agent-level skills within it are referenced by ID (fetch full
content via `/skills/{id}`).

roles.description: The roles this agent fills via primary, non-discarded assignments.

AgentContextRole.description: A role an agent fills — inline identity only, no definition.

circle_name.description: Name of the parent circle, if any.

SkillSummary.description: A skill as returned in list responses. Omits the full markdown `content` to keep list payloads small — fetch full content on demand via `GET /skills/{id}`.

tags.description: Tag names applied to this skill, sorted alphabetically. Tags are free-form strings organized by convention. The well-known `specialist` tag marks a skill as invokable by a sub-agent.

Skill.description: A skill including the full markdown body.

content.description: The full markdown content of the skill.

SkillDetail.description: A skill with optional included resources.

ChecklistItem.description: A checklist item on a role.

ChecklistItemInput.description: Input for creating or updating a checklist item.

MetricInput.description: Input for creating or updating a metric.

role_id.description: The role that owns this action.

individual_initiative.description: Whether the action is an individual initiative (not owned by a specific role).

parent_project_id.description: The api_id of the parent project, or null if not linked to a project.

tags.description: Tag names applied to this action.

focus.description: Optional focus area for the assignment.

ActionInput.description: Input for creating or updating an action.

individual_initiative.description: Whether the action is an individual initiative (not owned by a specific role).

parent_project_id.description: Set the parent project by api_id. Pass null to unlink.

Tension.description: A tension sensed by a role filler.

body.example: We ship work faster than we update the roadmap.

status.description:
Lifecycle state. `unprocessed` and `processed` are auto-computed from the
presence of associated actions/projects/proposals/agenda-items. Clients
can set `archived` explicitly via PATCH.

role_id.description: The role that sensed this tension (column `impacted_role_id`; semantically the sensing role per app convention).

sensed_by_id.description: The person who sensed and captured this tension.

parent_role_id.description: The role id of the parent role this tension belongs to, if any.

TensionInput.description: Input for creating or updating a tension.

Goal.description:
A goal (objective) on a role. Progress is computed on read as the mean
of kept target progresses, clamped to `[0, 100]`. When a goal has no
targets, progress is `null` (not `0`).

progress.description:
Mean of kept target progresses, rounded. `null` when the goal has
no targets. Targets the caller can't see are still counted in the
server-side rollup (the goal's progress is an org-level aggregate).

has_supporting_goals.description: Whether this goal has non-discarded child/supporting goals.

has_supporting_projects.description: Whether this goal has non-discarded, non-private supporting projects.

parent_goal_id.description:
The `api_id` of the parent goal, or `null` if there is no parent.
When multiple parents exist, returns one (non-deterministic).

targets.description:
Targets (key results) under this goal. Only present when
`?include=targets` is requested.

supporting_projects.description:
Projects linked as supporting this goal. Only present when
`?include=supporting_projects` is requested.

GoalInput.description: Input for creating or updating a goal.

Channel.description:
A chat channel — 1:1 with a Role. Circle-role channels are group
chats (members = circle role-fillers); leaf-role channels are
DM-like (members = the role's own filler(s)).

role_id.description: The bound role's api_id (any role — circle or leaf).

integration_data.description: Generic per-platform metadata container. Empty in this surface; populated by the multi-platform external-chat integration series (Slack/Teams/Discord adapters) to carry per-channel binding coordinates.

viewer_last_read_at.description: The caller's newest read watermark on this channel (across the person-level and any role-scoped marks). Null when the caller has never marked the channel read.

viewer_unread_count.description: Count of messages newer than the caller's watermark (all messages when the watermark is null).

role_id.description: Set when the watermark is role-scoped.

Message.description: A single post made by a Person into a Channel.

from_role_id.description: The role the sender posted as. Required for agent senders, optional for humans (auto-derived when the caller fills exactly one role in the channel's circle).

parent_id.description: Optional parent message for simple threading.

edited_at.description: Set when the body has been edited. This is the entire edit-history surface — messages carry no revision log.

body.description: The message body (plain text; formatting rules TBD).

from_role.description: The role to post as (api_id). Required for agents; optional for humans when unambiguous.

Target.description:
A target (key result) under a goal. Progress is computed on read via
`(current_value - starting_value) / (ending_value - starting_value) * 100`,
clamped to `[0, 100]`. Edge cases: starting/ending/current nulls → 0;
`ending_value == starting_value` → 100 if current ≥ ending else 0.

role_id.description:
The role the target is assigned to. May differ from the parent
goal's role (cross-circle target alignment is supported).

current_value.description:
The value from the latest kept progress update on this target.
Null when the target has no progress updates yet.

progress.description: Computed percentage (see schema description for formula and edge cases).

value_prefix.description: Optional unit prefix rendered before the value (e.g. `$`).

value_suffix.description: Optional unit suffix rendered after the value (e.g. `%`).

TargetInput.description: Input for creating or updating a target.

parent_id.description:
The parent goal or target's `api_id`. Type disambiguated via
the sibling `parent_type` field.

value.description: Required when `parent_type` is `target`. Optional for goals.

ProgressUpdateInput.description: Input for creating a progress update on a goal or target.

SkillInput.description: Input for creating or updating a skill.

tags.description: Tag names to apply to the skill (case-insensitive). On update, the supplied array replaces the full tag set; pass [] to clear all tags, omit to leave tags unchanged. The well-known `specialist` tag marks a skill as invokable by a sub-agent.

body.description: The strategy text. Null when no strategy is set and none is inherited.

inherited.description: True when the strategy is inherited from a parent circle.

inherited_from_role_id.description: The role ID of the parent circle this strategy is inherited from.

org_skills.description:
Index of every skill in the org library (id + name only). Lets agents
know what's available to load on demand via getSkill, beyond the
skills already linked to their role.

ContextAgent.description: Agent identity. Only present when the API key belongs to an agent.

skills.description: Agent-level skills (fetch full content via getSkill).

sections.description:
The six rule sections that define the organization's governance,
each with its chosen rule variant (HOLACRACY, UNIVERSAL,
CENTRALIZED, CUSTOM, EXISTING, MODULAR_ADOPTION_BY_CIRCLE) and
the corresponding rich content text.

type.description: Which rule variant the organization has adopted for this section.

summary.description:
Brief summary of the section. Present for HOLACRACY sections
(from locale). Absent for other types.

content.description:
Inline content for short sections. Present for
UNIVERSAL/CENTRALIZED/CUSTOM when text is under 500 characters,
and for MODULAR_ADOPTION_BY_CIRCLE. Null for EXISTING.
Absent for HOLACRACY (use content_url instead).

content_url.description:
URL to fetch the full section text. Present for HOLACRACY
sections and for UNIVERSAL/CENTRALIZED/CUSTOM sections with
content >= 500 characters.

mcp_tool.description:
MCP tool name to fetch the full section text on demand.
Present when content_url is present.

content.description: Full text of the section. Null for EXISTING.

skills.description: Role-level skills (fetch full content via getSkill).

notes.description: Notes on this role (title and excerpt).

ContextParentRole.description: The parent role this role belongs to, with its policies (null for anchor roles).

policies.description: Policies from this role and ancestor roles.

ancestor_roles.description: Chain of ancestor roles up to the anchor role.

sibling_roles.description: Other roles in the same parent role.

ContextIndexEntry.description:
A generic index entry pointing to a resource. Used throughout the context
response for progressive disclosure — each entry identifies a resource and
optionally links to its full-detail endpoint.

type.description: Resource type (role, policy, note, skill, project, action).

excerpt.description: Brief content excerpt (present for policies and notes).

url.description: API URL for full resource detail (when a v5 endpoint exists).

circle_id.description:
The `api_id` of the role that supports this proposal's circle.
v5 is role-centric — circle references resolve to the circle's
supported role.

response_summary.description:
Aggregate response counts. No per-person attribution is exposed —
this is an intentional anti-political-pressure design decision to
prevent back-channel pressure on whoever requested bring-to-meeting.

expected_response_count.description:
Number of circle members whose response is required for the
proposal to auto-accept. Excludes the proposer and anyone added
to the circle after `proposed_at`.

received_response_count.description:
Number of expected responders who have submitted a response.
When `received_response_count >= expected_response_count` and
no responder has `bring_to_meeting`, the cron auto-accepts.

available_transitions.description:
Action names this caller may invoke on this proposal right now.
Filtered by both current-state guards and caller authorization.
Each name maps to a path: `POST /proposals/{id}/<name>`.
Clients construct the URL — server returns names only.

ProposalChange.description:
A governance command (create role, add accountability, remove domain,
etc.). Shape varies by change type — `type` is always present; other
keys are free-form based on the command's schema.

Nested-only types (`CreateAccountability`, `UpdateAccountability`,
`RemoveAccountability`, `CreateDomain`, `UpdateDomain`,
`RemoveDomain`) must appear as children of `CreateRole` or
`UpdateRole`, not as top-level proposal changes.

id.description: Stable identifier for the change within the proposal.

ProposalVote.description:
A governance vote on a proposal. No per-person attribution —
summary stats only on the proposal resource.

proposal_status.description:
Current status of the parent proposal at the time of response.
Useful when the response triggers auto-acceptance — the status
will be `accepted` rather than `proposed_outside_meeting`.

value.description:
* `no_objection` — willing to let the proposal pass as written.
* `bring_to_meeting` — wants to discuss in a live governance
  meeting. Blocks auto-acceptance.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details error object (backward-compatible successor to RFC 7807). All 4xx and 5xx responses from the API use this shape. Additional members may be present as RFC 9457 "extensions".

type.description: A URI reference identifying the problem type. Defaults to `about:blank`.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this occurrence.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.

content_length.description: Extension member. Present on a 422 that rejects content for being too large. The size of the submitted content, in characters.

max_content_length.description: Extension member. Present on a 422 that rejects content for being too large. The size limit currently in effect, in characters.

limit_config_key.description: Extension member. Present on a 422 that rejects content for being too large. Names the server configuration key that produced `max_content_length`, so a limit that looks wrong can be traced to the setting that set it.

ContentSizeWarnings.description: Warnings about the saved record. Present only when there is something to report. Currently used for content that saved successfully but is too large for an agent to read in one response. Each warning names the content size, the limit, and the configuration key that set the limit.
example: Note body is 52000 characters. Agents cannot read content over 40000 characters in one response (config: GLASSFROG_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKEN_CAP).

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed — for example, `per_page` exceeds the maximum allowed value. The `detail` describes the specific issue.

Forbidden.description: Not authorized to perform this action.

NotFound.description: Resource not found or API v5 not enabled for this organization.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with the current state of the resource —
for example, a business-rule violation or an ETag mismatch
(resource modified since the `If-Match` value; re-fetch and retry).

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded. The `Retry-After` header indicates how many seconds to wait before retrying.

example.title: Too Many Requests
example.detail: Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 42 seconds.
